title: Moroni reads Helaman’s report
summary: After reading Helaman’s epistle, Moroni rejoices at Helaman’s success and makes the news known to the people around him.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni received and read Helaman’s epistle and rejoiced at Helaman’s success in obtaining lost lands.
Moroni made the news known to the people in the surrounding land so they could rejoice.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni can be shown reading a letter and then sharing its news with nearby people.
unspecified_visual_details: The epistle’s appearance and contents beyond the reported success.
The precise location, clothing, and appearance of Moroni and the people.

narration.text: he did make it known unto all his people

prohibited_inventions: Do not show Helaman present; the source only mentions his epistle.

title: Moroni writes to Pahoran
summary: Moroni sends an epistle to Pahoran requesting men to strengthen Helaman’s forces, then plans to recover the remaining possessions and cities held by the Lamanites.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni sent Pahoran an epistle requesting men to strengthen Helaman’s armies.
After sending the epistle to Zarahemla, Moroni began planning to obtain the remaining possessions and cities taken by the Lamanites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni can be shown writing or dispatching an epistle, followed by considering a plan.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether Pahoran receives or reads the epistle.
The letter’s appearance, Moroni’s surroundings, and the details of his plan.

narration.text: he immediately sent an epistle to Pahoran
he began again to lay a plan

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Pahoran responding or men assembling; neither event is stated.

title: The people of Nephihah are attacked
summary: While Moroni prepares to battle the Lamanites, the Lamanites attack the gathered people of Nephihah and begin to slay them. People who had fled Manti and the surrounding land had previously joined the Lamanites.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni was preparing to battle the Lamanites while the attack occurred.
The people of Nephihah had gathered from the cities of Moroni, Lehi, and Morianton and were attacked by the Lamanites.
People compelled to flee Manti and the surrounding land had joined the Lamanites.
The Lamanites were exceedingly numerous, received strength from day to day, and, by Ammoron's command, came against the people of Nephihah and began to slay them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lamanites' attack and the beginning of the slaughter may be depicted as physical action without gore.
unspecified_visual_details: The participants' exact appearances and numbers.
The precise location and terrain of the attack.

narration.text: the people of Nephihah, who were gathered together from the city of Moroni and the city of Lehi and the city of Morianton, were attacked by the Lamanites.
by the command of Ammoron they came forth against the people of Nephihah, and they did begin to slay them with an exceedingly great slaughter.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Moroni's preparations occur while the attack takes place; the verses do not place him at the attack.
The flight from Manti and the joining of the Lamanites are prior events, not actions occurring during this attack.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Moroni or Ammoron as present at the attack.
Do not reenact the earlier flight from Manti within this scene.
Do not add dialogue, gore, or identities for unnamed people.

title: Survivors flee and join Moroni
summary: The remaining people of Nephihah flee the numerous Lamanite army and join Moroni’s army. Moroni had expected Nephihah to be reinforced and retained his force to hold the places he had recovered.

explicit_facts.text: The remainder of Nephihah’s people fled before the Lamanites and joined Moroni’s army.
Moroni expected men to be sent to assist Nephihah and supposed the city would be maintained.
Moroni retained his force to maintain the places he had recovered.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The flight from Nephihah can be shown as people leaving the city; Moroni’s army may be shown as their destination.
unspecified_visual_details: The route from Nephihah to Moroni’s army and the army’s precise location.
Whether Moroni is visibly present as the people arrive.

narration.text: the remainder of the people of Nephihah were obliged to flee
they came even and joined the army of Moroni

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the expected reinforcements arriving; the source says Moroni supposed they would be sent.

title: Moroni learns Nephihah is lost
summary: When Moroni sees that Nephihah is lost, he is sorrowful and doubts whether the people will fall into the hands of their enemies. His chief captains share the doubt and wonder at the Lamanite success.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni saw that Nephihah was lost, became sorrowful, and began to doubt because of the people’s wickedness.
Moroni’s chief captains also doubted and marveled at the Lamanites’ success over them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni and his captains can be shown reacting with sorrow and uncertainty.
unspecified_visual_details: How Moroni learned or what evidence he saw that Nephihah was lost.
The captains’ identities, number, and exact setting.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the loss of Nephihah as a separate present-tense event in this scene.

title: Moroni’s anger at the government
summary: Moroni becomes angry with the government over its indifference concerning the freedom of the country.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni was angry with the government because of its indifference concerning the freedom of the country.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni may be shown expressing anger.
unspecified_visual_details: The government’s members, location, and any exchange between them and Moroni.

narration.text: Moroni was angry with the government

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict government members or invent a confrontation; neither is described.
